identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian customer sports prototype built by Metalmoro, sold in several prototype classes. The manufacturer states the car accepts a choice of engine and gearbox rather than specifying either. Honda denotes the engine.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip on downshifts. The downshift was accepted with no pedal input, so no blip is needed to engage the gear.
The clutch is not needed to pull away.

Shares the P3 class with the MRX Duratec Turbo P3 and pulls away without the clutch where that car needs it. Both were driven separately. The two agree on the automatic blip: neither car blips its own downshifts.

Metalmoro states only that the MRX accepts several engine and gearbox options, so no reviewed source establishes which gearbox this configuration carries. The sequential construction is what the drive showed.
Community references for this car are generated from Coanda's AMS2 spreadsheet, so they describe the simulator rather than the real car and are not cited here as real-world evidence.
The car does not blip its own downshifts. An earlier drive recorded that it did, from a measurement that could read the driver's throttle as the car's blip.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.metalmoro-mrx-honda-p3.20260817t043937857z-3caf7179 by Jason Kinslow.

The automatic blip was re-measured on 2026-08-18 in AMS2 1.6.9.91, observation ams2.metalmoro-mrx-honda-p3.20260818t041859673z-d8236075. The car does not blip: the first reading was the old measurement seeing throttle carried in before the lift. The downshift was still accepted with no pedal input, so no blip is needed to engage the gear.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

claims.basis: The manufacturer's own page establishes the MRX; the class and engine configuration were observed live.
The manufacturer does not state a gearbox, so the six sequential gears and the automatic cut come from the live drive rather than from the source.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: The guided drive pulled away with no clutch input, where the archetype's cars need it. Metalmoro states only that the MRX accepts a choice of gearbox, so no reviewed source establishes which one this configuration carries and the sequential construction is what the drive showed.
